title: Environment Variables [PATH]
description:
# PATH
`$PATH` is the most important environment variable. It tells your shell WHERE to look for programs.

When you type `ls`, the shell doesn't magically know where `ls` lives. It searches every directory in `$PATH` left to right until it finds it.

```bash
echo $PATH
# /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
```

Directories are separated by `:`. The shell checks `/usr/local/bin` first, then `/usr/bin`, then `/bin`, etc.

### Useful commands:
```bash
which ls        # shows where ls lives
which python3   # shows where python3 lives
```

### Adding to PATH:
```bash
export PATH="$PATH:/my/new/directory"
```
This appends your directory to the end.
